paragraphs.source_en: While Ban Dan’emon fought alone, Ōno Harufusa had not even set out; he was still at Gansenji Temple in Kaizuka. Bokuhansai once again brought out sake to reward the troops, and Harufusa gladly gave himself over to the drinking. Yet he was not wholly lost in the wine; he had another scheme in mind.

paragraphs.source_en: Harufusa spoke this way because he had already sent two veteran retainers, Kitamura Kitayū and Ōno Yagoemon, with a band of men to infiltrate the outskirts of Wakayama Castle. He had ordered them to lie in wait until Asano Nagaakira came out of the castle, then seize the moment and take the empty stronghold in one stroke. He was waiting there for good news from the two men. By his reckoning, the fact that the vanguard commander Ban Dan’emon had encountered the enemy at the front meant that Wakayama Castle was already empty and could be taken without the slightest effort.

paragraphs.source_en: Harufusa stood dumbstruck, unable to utter a word. He had nowhere to advance or retreat, for they had burned and plundered everything along the road behind them; if they remained where they were, they would have to endure hunger.
